report.clinical_summary: The patient presented with a solitary, painless pea-sized lump in the submandibular region (under the chin) that has been present for about a month without change in size or shape. The lump is mobile, firm but not tender, and not associated with any other neck swelling or recent dental issues. Fatigue has been present for about two weeks, worse after work, described as physical tiredness with reduced energy and slower recovery from exercise. No night sweats, temperature changes, or other associated symptoms. The patient is not on any medication and has no chronic conditions. Examination findings: neck lump is firm, mobile, non-tender; thyroid is normal in size and smooth; no other lymphadenopathy noted. Assessment: neck lump is most likely benign; fatigue is non-specific. Plan: watchful waiting for neck lump with monthly self-examination; lifestyle changes for fatigue; blood work if symptoms worsen.
